canonical_subtitle: A thought experiment on admissibility, governance, action, and the uniqueness of an observed state transition

core_formalism.uniqueness_rule: Once admissibility, governance, and the applied action are sufficiently specified, the collapse resolves to one eigenvalue corresponding to the observed successor manifold O.
core_formalism.residual_multiplicity_rule: If more than one eigenvalue remains, the reconstruction is insufficient because some discriminating part of the manifold state, governance matrix, admissibility matrix, or action matrix remains unaccounted for.
core_formalism.continuity_rule: Continuity exists when preserved information is sufficient to reconstruct why the action on N, under its governance and admissibility structure, could collapse only to O.
core_formalism.scale_rule: As the manifold grows, the concrete matrices become larger and more coupled, but the governing structure remains (Admissibility, Governance, Action) -> one eigenvalue -> successor manifold.
core_formalism.working_term_boundary: Eigenvalue is working formalism naming the unique resolved value of the combined transition problem; the exact operator and spectral interpretation remain to be formalized.

compact_formulation: Reconstruct manifold state N and its admissibility and governance structures.
Identify the action matrix actually applied to N.
Collapse admissibility against governance under that action.
Require one eigenvalue corresponding to the observed successor O.
Preserve O and its new admissibility matrix as the next manifold state.
Treat residual multiplicity as evidence of insufficient reconstruction.
